title: Leviticus Bible Quiz - Chapter 27
description: Ten questions on Leviticus 27: valuations for vows, redeeming what is dedicated, and the tithe that is holy to Yahweh.

questions.text: What was the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old consecrated in a vow?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 sets the valuation of such a male at fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

questions.text: What was the valuation of a male from a month old to five years old?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says the valuation for such a male is five shekels of silver, and for a female three shekels.

questions.text: What happened if the person who made the vow was poorer than the valuation?
questions.explanation: He was set before the priest, who assigned a value according to his ability to pay.

answers.text: The priest assigned a value according to his ability to pay
He was released from his vow without paying
He served in the sanctuary for the remaining amount
His nearest relative paid the rest of the valuation

questions.text: What happened if someone exchanged one animal given to Yahweh for another?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says that if he exchanges animal for animal, both it and the one it was exchanged for shall be holy.

answers.text: The first animal was given back
The priest chose the better one

questions.text: What did a man have to add if he wanted to redeem the house he had dedicated?
questions.explanation: If he redeems his house, he shall add the fifth part of the money of the valuation, and it shall be his.

answers.text: A tenth part of the valuation
The fifth part of the valuation

questions.text: How was the valuation of a dedicated field from a man's possession set?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says the valuation shall be according to the seed for it; the sowing of a homer of barley was valued at fifty shekels of silver.

answers.text: According to the seed for it
By the number of its trees
By its distance from the city
By the size of its well

questions.text: If a dedicated field was not redeemed, who would own it when it went out in the Jubilee?
questions.explanation: It would be holy to Yahweh as a devoted field, and it would be owned by the priests.

questions.text: How many gerahs make up the shekel of the sanctuary?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 says all valuations shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs to the shekel.

questions.text: Why could no man dedicate a firstborn ox or sheep?
questions.explanation: The firstborn among animals belongs to Yahweh as a firstborn: "It is Yahweh's."

answers.text: Because it already belongs to Yahweh
Because it belongs to the priest's family
Because it must first be sold

questions.text: Which animals of the herds and flocks are holy to Yahweh as the tithe?
questions.explanation: Of whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to Yahweh; the owner shall not examine whether it is good or bad.

answers.text: The best one chosen by the owner
The tenth that passes under the rod
The seventh one born each year
The largest male of the flock
